existing_questions: why is a cpu flame graph insufficient by itself to explain a request delayed by blocking?

a team adds a search store beside its transactional database and updates both stores in the request path. a request reports success but the document is later missing from search, a rebuild follows a mapping change, and one replay delivers the same change twice. why is a successful double write not evidence that the two representations agree, which invariants must be owned before the search view may serve reads, and what does the outbox commit and not commit?
what can a missing sampled trace tell an investigator about a possibly committed write?
what relationship details must be defined before interpreting a graph edge?

a team resharding from 16 to 17 modulo buckets finds that nearly every key remaps, so it adopts a consistent-hashing ring and raises virtual nodes per node from 64 to 512. why does the ring bound movement, and why can more tokens still worsen failure and repair outcomes rather than making ownership safer?
why is a confidence interval across synthetic replications not a calibrated input uncertainty budget?
why does reciprocal rank fusion add only rank reciprocals rather than the underlying lexical and semantic scores, and what does the k constant control?
why is p99 latency not a valid substitute for mean residence time in little’s law?

a team edits an accepted architecture decision record in place so it describes the option it eventually chose, and cites a closed documentation issue as approval. why does that destroy the decision trail, and what must the record and any superseding record state instead?

a v12 discrete-event run satisfies offered = completed + rejected + failed + in_system after every replication. why does that identity still not prove each request was assigned the correct outcome, and which checks cover the outcome path instead?
how is a rollback duration reported when the modeled drain has not completed by the end of the horizon?
how are correlated lag and reconciliation-capacity assumptions propagated in the v12 modernization scenario?
how does a v12 decision record treat a failed hard constraint compared with a soft preference?
why can an evenly distributed shard set still leave one tenant on an overloaded shard, and what must a resharding move preserve?

a scheduled availability probe passes for a checkout journey while customers receive rejects, and when the probe does fail the alert fires only after three successive failures. why can a green probe coexist with a broken user journey, why does the retry rule suppress a real signal, and what must the probe declare before its result is used as evidence?
what extra recovery coordination can a continuously reconciling gitops controller require during an emergency rollback?
why does filtering a malicious instruction out of retrieved text not make an assistant's later tool call authorized, and where must the authorization check occur?
why does restoring a consistent stream-processing checkpoint not prove that an external side effect happened exactly once?
why is an exact nearest-neighbor scan insufficient to certify an approximate index after the embedding model changes?
how does the v12 engine prevent a completion event that was scheduled before a timeout from freeing a server a second time?

candidate a has the lower p95 latency, yet the v12 comparative record recommends candidate b. why is that not a contradiction, and which part of the recommendation is a value judgment rather than a simulated fact?
how should a stock-flow model account for offered work at every integration step?
after every participant votes to prepare, why can a two-phase commit stay undecided, and why must a prepared participant wait rather than resolve it alone?
why can horizontal autoscaling fail to prevent overload during a burst even when the controller eventually selects the correct replica count?
when may an expanded database schema be contracted during a mixed-version rollout?
in shopify’s 2019 componentization account, how did wedge surface cross-component dependencies?
what must happen before an old region can safely regain authority after failover?

a read projector is rebuilt from the beginning of the event log after a mapping change, and the same projector also sends confirmation email for every event it applies. why must the rebuild suppress those side effects and commit the view and cursor together, and when may the rebuilt view serve queries as current?
why is r + w > n necessary but not sufficient for a quorum read to return the newest acknowledged write?
why can a chain of per-hop timeouts that are each individually reasonable still outlive the caller's end-to-end deadline?

a three-voter metadata store is expanded to four voters to improve resilience, and reads and writes continue to use r + w > n. why does the fourth voter add no failure tolerance while raising the commit quorum, and why can a read still be stale during the membership change?
why can a component inventory produced from a source checkout fail to establish the component set of the released container image?

a scenario overrides the server count declared by its model, and the model's calibration note still records the original assumed value. the run executes and the structural checks pass. why is the run's evidence status ambiguous rather than invalid?
why is a valid signature over build provenance for one artifact digest insufficient to authorize promoting an image that currently has the same tag?

a long-running durable workflow is upgraded while thousands of histories are mid-flight, and an activity that sends a confirmation email is retried after a worker crash. why can the upgrade and the retry each corrupt the workflow's meaning, what must replay and activity idempotency guarantee, and why is a completed workflow state not proof that the external effect happened?
when should an architecture experiment stop instead of drawing a conclusion from apparently favorable latency?
why does a v12 decision record link one way to existing pattern identifiers instead of writing a backlink into the pattern card, and what does such a link not establish?
why can an index assembled from document revisions that never coexisted produce misleading evidence?
why does limiting a canary to five percent of traffic not bound the fraction of old-version readers that can encounter an incompatible new state?
why can an index that helped one tenant make the same query slower for another, and which conditions must be fixed before the two access paths are compared?
what evidence status does a v12 input carry when it is computed from one measured and one assumed value, and what can change that status?

a platform sells a tenant 100 requests per second but enforces it with a 100-token-per-second bucket in each of six replicas. under uneven routing the tenant exceeds the sold rate, and during a quota-store outage the replicas keep admitting. why is the sold limit not enforced, and what must the limiter contract state about scope, accounting failure and the difference between rate and concurrency?
why is mirrored production traffic unsafe for a shadow service that performs live writes?
why can a highly selective metadata filter leave an approximate nearest-neighbor query short of the k results it requested?
why can adding more workers past some point reduce throughput under the universal scalability law, and why do the fitted coefficients not identify the cause?
why is a local read model a poor substitute for a synchronous dependency when every read requires strong consistency?
why is 'twenty requests per second of backlog' not a coherent state description, and what must be true before backlog divided by throughput can be read as a time?
when can an in-place runtime upgrade address a modernization problem without moving data ownership?
what does a bounded platform worker pool fail to bound when its submission queue is unlimited?
what must a transactional outbox relay do after a state change commits but publication has not yet happened?
why does a subscriber's bounded request(n) not by itself protect a reactive service from overload?
why must a parallel-run comparison preserve an authoritative old result while testing a candidate?
why can a duplicate read sent to a second replica shorten the tail while increasing the load that produced the tail?
why can a validly signed build attestation for an artifact digest still fail to establish that the artifact is eligible for release?
how does the v12 quadratic sensitivity screen differ from a full sobol analysis?
in netflix’s cloud migration retrospective, what failure helped motivate reconstruction instead of lifting the existing application unchanged?
what artifacts are needed for a physical point-in-time restore using postgresql wal?
what must be fixed in advance to compare two architecture changes without shifting the decision criterion after the test?
why does v12 keep a two-replication convergence-stress run that fails the 0.02 relative-error threshold instead of discarding it or reporting it as converged?

two checkout candidates' 95% intervals overlap on success rate, so the review records no difference and keeps the cheaper candidate. why is that an insufficient-evidence outcome rather than evidence of equivalence, and what must the record state instead?

a device-status stream drops after the server sends sequence 41 but before the consumer acknowledges it, and the client reconnects with the last sequence it durably processed. why can the resumed stream still contain duplicates or a gap, and what must the stream contract define before resume is a supported guarantee?
why can a closed-loop load generator report low latency and low throughput while an independent arrival stream would overload the same service?
which analytic monte carlo checks are identified as future work rather than completed reference tests?
why does embedding sqlite in an application not by itself provide a networked multi-region database service?
why does advancing a watermark past a window not make its published total final, and what must the processing contract declare before a late booking correction is applied?

a team shortens a dns record's ttl to 30 seconds before removing a failed endpoint, yet some clients keep sending requests to that endpoint for several minutes. why does the ttl not bound how long clients use the old endpoint, and what must the cutover plan establish before the endpoint is retired?

a team replaces an in-process reservation repository adapter with a remote service behind the same application port, and the port's contract tests still pass. why is interface conformance insufficient to prove the substitution safe, and what must the adapter contract and tests add?

a three-stage pipeline validates an order, writes an audit record, and publishes a confirmation. after the audit record commits, the confirmation stage fails before publishing, and the broker redelivers the original message a day later. why does the pipeline's non-transactional filter fail to preserve the completed stage, and what must the stage identity, ordering scope and recovery checkpoint record so the redelivery neither duplicates the audit record nor loses the confirmation?
why is an audit trail unreliable if the actor being audited can modify or delete the records?
how can a client recover the status of a submitted job when the initial acknowledgment is lost?
why do a missed lease renewal and an expired timeout both leave the outcome uncertain, and what must happen before either is treated as settled?
why can a virtual thread blocked inside a synchronized block pin a carrier on jdk 21 but not on jdk 24, and which blocking paths can still pin?

an operations team replaces every slo alert with a single five-minute burn-rate threshold and pauses releases whenever it fires. why can that rule both page on noise and miss a slow budget leak, and what must the decision establish before any burn-rate threshold is trusted?
how can retries distort the denominator of a user-facing service indicator?
what can a consumer offset reset to earliest recover after older kafka records have expired?
why can a locally passing v12 validator not substitute for the v12-f review gate, and what does that gate still not establish?
why do additional replicas not automatically increase a single authoritative shard’s write capacity?

a team deletes retired customer records from its primary audit store, but a backup archive, a search index and an old incident export still contain them. why does the primary deletion not satisfy the retention or erasure obligation, and what must the retention design inventory and govern?

a simulation measures a steady-state p95 from a window that starts at time zero, although the model starts empty and its queue fills during the first minutes. why does that window bias the estimate, what must the scenario declare and the engine enforce about warmup, and why does convergence not repair the bias?
what did netflix’s chaos kong regional simulation leave outside the tested failure envelope?
what controls can make module ownership enforceable inside a single deployable?

a new retriever returns several relevant documents that no earlier system retrieved and that the judgment pool never judged. why can its recall@k look worse than the system whose results built the pool, and what must be re-run before the two are compared?

a change-data-capture connector completes its initial snapshot and streams row changes, then its replication slot falls behind retention and is dropped. why did the snapshot not prove the derived state was complete, and what must be recorded so that a rebuild stays bounded?

a program labels every integration a service, routes all calls through one central bus that applies transformations and business rules, and cannot name a contract version or a consumer for any capability. why does the atlas reject this use of soa, what must a governed service contract declare, and when are microservices or a modular monolith the better comparison?
what is the difference between an observed service indicator and its objective?

a booking service replaces its limited-seat approval rule with a mergeable set so disconnected approvers can synchronize automatically. why can the replicas converge on the same state while the approval limit is still violated, and what must happen to authority-dependent approvals?
why can a java process exceed a memory limit while heap occupancy looks stable?
why can twelve routes, five outcome classes, three regions and forty instances produce 7,200 metric series, and why does that series count not determine ingest volume?

two regions accept writes to the same customer record and replicate asynchronously; a profile edit and an address deletion arrive in either order, the system resolves by last-write timestamp, and reconciliation later restores the deleted address. why is timestamp resolution not a sufficient conflict contract, why does synchronous multi-master not escape the conflict cost, and when must multi-leader be rejected?

a daily booking total is computed in event time; event e5 arrives after the watermark has closed its window, and a later cancellation must change the total. why is finalization at the watermark not proof that earlier events are complete, and what must the lateness and correction contract decide before the total is treated as settled?
why should a liveness probe not restart a healthy process merely because a shared dependency is unavailable?
why is telling an assistant to ignore instructions found in retrieved documents insufficient, and where must the boundary be enforced instead?
in meta’s ingestion migration, where did the candidate job write during the initial shadow phase?
why does a p95 checkout latency comparison require request-level events rather than only a fluid model?
why does replacing a failed worker in a shuffle-sharded pool not restore the isolation the assignment promised?
why are a database log position, a kafka partition offset, a processor checkpoint and an external sink commit not interchangeable as recovery cursors?

a proposed index lowers a query's estimated plan cost and the planner chooses an index scan. why does that not establish lower user latency, and which lifecycle costs decide whether the index is a net improvement?

a team doubles its largest instance size after a 3x traffic forecast, sees throughput rise by less than half, schedules a restart for the resize, and plans to repeat the doubling next year. why is that not a capacity plan, what must be measured and bounded before the next resize, and when does the card reverse to horizontal scaling?

a team replaces a join with an application-maintained index table and adds a covering column so the lookup avoids the base table. why can the lookup return a stale or wrong row even though the base table is correct, and what must the write path and key preserve?
why does full jitter reduce synchronized retry waves, and why must a model record its jitter policy to be reproducible?
why can a cpu-utilization autoscaler reduce replica count while request latency is rising, and what should be examined instead?

three api replicas are spread across zones a and b, but every replica authorizes through one zone-a identity endpoint and commits through one zone-a database writer. after zone a fails, why can the zone-b replicas report healthy processes yet complete no bookings, and what must the availability claim state instead?
why does the v12 result hash include limitations and convergence information along with metrics?

two client applications share one general-purpose api, and each filters fields and makes several calls. why can a per-client backend improve the contract without becoming a second domain authority, and what release risk appears when it deploys independently?
what alternative can reduce comparison overhead when running two implementations in parallel is too costly?
why does a parent that waits for ten independent dependency calls exceed its latency threshold far more often than any single child's p99 suggests?

a whitespace-only reformat of a model file makes v12 replay fail, while a whitespace-only reformat of the stored run record leaves its result hash unchanged. why does v12 treat the two artifacts differently, and what does each hash identify?
what does the v12 engine do when the queue or bulkhead reaches its admission limit?
why does a 100% target traffic share not establish that a cutover succeeded?
why can a visible backlog look stable while total work grows, and what must a stock-and-flow model do about stocks that sit outside its boundary?
every participant votes yes, then the coordinator crashes before recording its decision. why can no participant safely commit or abort on its own, and what must the recovery decision be based on?
when is a planned controlled cutover unsuitable because an essential source-side condition cannot be met?

a v12 decision record cites a stable pattern identifier and its canonical owner page, and the derived reverse index lists that pattern next to the decision. what does the link actually establish, and why must it not be read as promotion, validation or a second canonical explanation of the pattern?
what runtime dependency did airbnb’s generated bazel targets sometimes miss during its gradle migration?
what infrastructure must exist before envoy can use the service-discovery approach described by the card?

when two simultaneous submissions reuse one idempotency key and the first commits while its response is lost, why is a read-then-insert check insufficient, and what must happen when the key returns with different parameters or after retention ends?
why can a service become overloaded while rejecting most incoming requests?

a capacity plan divides 3,050 operations from one hour into 0.85 operations per second, while a 15-second claim window actually receives 1,800 attempts on a few keys. why does the hour average mis-size that service, and which demand quantities must stay distinct?
why is a normal-approximation confidence interval acceptable for the v12 success rate but risky for its p95 latency?
why can removing an origin asset leave an old copy available after an edge purge?
why can a session token guarantee read-your-writes without making stored data globally consistent, and what must happen when that token cannot survive failover?
why do ordered lamport clock values not prove a causal relationship between two events?
why must a cached absence or denial be scoped to a principal and a policy revision rather than to an object identifier alone?
why must a scatter-gather fix a completeness rule and a straggler policy before it can return an answer, and what must the response disclose about participants that did not reply?

to cut server connections, a team switches a long-lived application from session pooling to pgbouncer transaction pooling. prepared statements and session-scoped commands then fail intermittently under concurrency. why does the pool mode change semantics rather than only connection reuse, and what must be pinned and tested before the switch?
why can three replicas spread across two zones still lose the booking journey together, and what must a recovery test demonstrate beyond healthy processes?

a capacity review computes a fleet p99 by averaging each instance's p99, keeps only hourly rollups after seven days, and then reports that a ten-minute queue crisis did not affect the tail. why can each step produce a false improvement, and what must be retained or recomputed before that claim is made?

a checkout team keeps enlarging its simulation by adding a cache model, a database model and a deployment model, because it assumes that a more detailed model is a more accurate one. why can the added detail fail to improve the decision, and what test should each proposed addition pass before its verification burden is accepted?
which extra isolation concern remains when tenants share a connection pool but data permissions are correct?

a v12 model declares its state variable in requests while its dynamics equation uses a rate, and the contract still passes the strict schema and the structural checks. why do the required unit fields not prevent that mismatch, and what does the contract claim to provide instead?
how does the v12 event queue break ties between events scheduled at the same time?
what does the v12 reference engine do when an invariant fails before a run record is written?
why can a higher recall@5 fail to justify a retrieval change, and what must lexical, vector or hybrid candidates share before their ranking metrics are comparable?

a team replicates its full stack into six regional stamps and routes tenants through a directory; the stamps share one identity service and one primary database, and each stamp is upgraded by hand. why does the replication not satisfy the stamp invariant, what must be enumerated and owned before isolation is claimed, and when is a cell-based design the better comparison?
when object bytes are stored outside the metadata database, why is a successfully verified upload not yet safe to expose to readers?

an alerting policy pages on a five-minute error-budget burn-rate window during normal traffic noise, but a one-hour window misses a slow and severe budget drain. why can neither window alone support the alert, and what must the policy establish before its threshold is treated as evidence?
what risk arises when a translation layer between legacy and new domains has no owner for its mappings?
when does the atlas prefer structured logs with request ids over distributed tracing?
why is dedicated static content hosting a poor fit for personalized content that cannot be cached?
why does a bounded queue smooth a brief burst but fail to create sustainable processing capacity?
after the modeled rollback trigger, where does the v12 modernization model send new traffic?
how can unfinished work at the end of an observation window distort a queueing estimate?
why does endpoint discovery still need active health checks?
what needs coordination when a tenant moves from shared storage to a dedicated database?
how should a reachability query bound path explosion in a cyclic graph?
under postgresql repeatable read, why can two transactions that both find no conflicting reservation still commit overlapping accepted bookings?

a team doubles a topic's partition count and changes the key encoding during a migration, expecting per-customer ordering to survive because every event still carries a customer key. why can ordering break even though each event is keyed, and what must the migration define before consumers rely on the new layout?
when is polling a separate asynchronous status resource unnecessary for a client?
what kind of request should not be retried automatically by an ambassador proxy without an effect-safety contract?

a reviewer treats an uncalibrated v12 model as an incomplete contract and demands a calibration number before the run may be cited. why is 'uncalibrated' a complete declared status, and what does that run remain licensed to support?

a dashboard computes each instance's p99 for a day and then averages those daily p99 values into a monthly figure. why can the result understate the latency most requests experience, and what must be kept so the latency distributions can be merged correctly?
why does a split message require an owned completion or partial-release rule when the number of parts is unknown?
why does a single-flight guard inside each replica fail to bound origin load when one hot cache key expires, and what would bound it?
why must workload identity be paired with an authorization policy before a caller's operations are allowed?
which edge-hosting responsibilities must be owned before static content is offloaded?

a client pages through a list ordered by creation time with a keyset cursor while rows are inserted and one caller's access to a row is revoked. why does the keyset cursor avoid offset drift without giving a stable snapshot, and what must the cursor bind so a stale page cannot expose the revoked row?

a server shutting down sends goaway with last-stream id 5 while one client connection still carries stream 5 (a publish whose response was lost) and stream 7 (which the peer never processed). why is it wrong to retry both streams the same way, and what must the client and the draining instance do before the instance is removed?

a twelve-node cache ring using consistent hashing gains a thirteenth node during peak traffic; the team expects only a small fraction of keys to move, yet the primary database saturates and one tenant's key range stays hot. why does bounded key movement not bound the load the origin sees, what does a higher virtual-node count change and what does it not change, and what must the rebalance own before it is admitted?
why can a minority partition of a five-voter raft group not commit new log entries?
why must a consumer tolerate duplicate publication when an outbox relay crashes after sending?
what evidence must a v12 model contract attach to an input labeled measured?
why is the age of an application insufficient evidence that its architecture caused an incident?
in a federation, why must a resource server check that an access token was issued for it rather than accept any token signed inside a trust chain?
why can a read that contacts a quorum of replicas still return a stale value after a write was acknowledged?
what evidence should gate an irreversible migration of authoritative state?
why does v12 fix the replication count in the scenario instead of stopping the run when the relative-error threshold is reached?
what must be verifiable before the controlled cutover card recommends pausing writes and switching authority?
why can a ttl shorter than the business freshness requirement still be rejected when a hard read-after-write contract exists?

a zero-server boundary case runs to completion without raising an error and is recorded as pass. why is that record not a verification result, and what must distinguish a boundary test from a smoke test?

two offline replicas each approve a different person for the last remaining seat and merge by last-writer timestamp. why can the merged state converge while the capacity invariant is already broken, and what must happen to an authority-dependent approval instead?

a server sends http/2 goaway with last-stream id 5 while stream 5 carried a publish that may already have committed at the state owner. why does the missing response not prove the effect failed, what does the boundary say about stream 7, and what must a bounded drain record before forced termination?
what limits the exposure from a leaked credential issued for direct storage access?
what environment details are recorded for replay, and what cross-platform guarantee do they not provide?
when is it acceptable for a v12 model to omit a dependency such as the payment network or the database, and what must the scope statement record so the omission is reviewable rather than hidden?

under overload a service replaces an empty recommendation result with a response formatted exactly like a complete one, and the degraded path has never run in production. why is that mode unsafe, what must its entry condition, visible status and recovery hysteresis declare, and why is an explicit error sometimes the better outcome?
why does a failed coordinator leave prepared participants holding locks, and why must one durable decision exist before any participant applies the outcome?
why is an authenticated tenant identifier insufficient to authorize a particular object?

during a rolling deploy, the platform removes an instance from the load balancer and sends the shutdown signal immediately. clients on long-lived http/2 connections see resets, and one publish is reported as failed even though it may have committed. why is removal from discovery not a drain, and what sequence and record must the operator require?
why can a full-text index that contains a document still fail to match the exact api identifier the document contains, and what must be pinned so matching does not drift?
what disposition should be specified for messages that arrive after a resequencer has advanced past a gap?
what consistency relation should hold between first-order and total-order sensitivity shares?

a shared cache stores a 404 for a document lookup and a 403 for a caller who lacked access. the document is later created and shared with that caller, and the policy revision changes. why can both cached negatives remain wrong after the change, and what must each key and lifetime bind?
why is an omitted dependency acceptable in a model boundary only when it cannot change the comparison under the declared conditions?

after a rolling restart, a dashboard that differences cumulative request counters shows a brief negative rate and then a traffic collapse, and the team concludes that capacity was lost. why is the counter reading not a business event, and what must the pipeline and query preserve to make the interval usable?
why can a trace set be adequate for diagnosing one slow request yet invalid for estimating how often requests are slow?
why do more simulation replications not remove uncertainty about the input distribution?
why can a model contract pass every automated check and still misstate its evidence?
when does a simulated output require batch means instead of the independent-replication standard error?

a model file has a unique tycho.model identifier and passes the strict schema, but no scenario or decision references it. why does structural validation still accept the file, and why is the file not evidence?
why must a claim-check token be published only after the payload write, and which failures remain after that ordering is enforced?
why must a compensating transaction carry its own authorization, evidence and failure mode rather than undo the failed step?

a tool catalogue stores one asset_code that means a shared model in one business area and a single physical unit in another. the migration copies the old code into new model_id and unit_id columns, reports equal source and target row counts, and starts serving reads from the new columns. why can this additive change corrupt reservations, and what must the migration do with identities it cannot prove and with writes that arrive during the backfill?
in netflix’s 2024 gc account, how could request pauses amplify load beyond the original slow request?
why can a cached not-found keep hiding an object after it has been created, and what must a negative cache key include before a denial may be shared?
why can a larger bounded queue lower the rejection rate while increasing the share of requests lost to timeouts?
when should a message router be preferred to a pass-or-discard filter?
why is a saga's compensating action not a rollback, and what must the workflow preserve when that compensation fails?
how can a v12 decision be decision-supported when every model input remains assumed?

a sensitivity screen reports that service mean explains more fitted variance than arrival rate, and the team proposes to cancel the planned service-time measurement because the model already shows what matters. why is that inference invalid, and what is the ranking legitimately used for?
a dual-write lag input for the modernization model has no defensible measured value. why does substituting zero yield a precise but meaningless result, and what must the decision record do instead?
why does committing an update fail to make the replaced row version immediately reclaimable, and what keeps vacuum from reusing its space?
why can an added api field be wire-compatible but incompatible with an old client’s business behavior?
how can stable component identifiers keep architecture views coherent without building a separate graph service?
what dependency makes write-triggered cache invalidation unsuitable when changes cannot be reliably signaled?
what should happen to the user response if the candidate fails during a parallel run?
why can a retry budget enforced independently at several layers still amplify offered load beyond the budget of any one layer?
why does a monotonic fencing token protect a resource only when the destination stores the highest accepted epoch atomically?
what kinds of identifiers, links and hashes does the v12 structural gate check?
what should operators plan for when a poison row prevents an outbox relay from progressing?
why does placing a service copy in every region not remove the failover problem, and what must be established before the old regional writer is replaced?
when does an open circuit breaker hide the underlying fault instead of containing it?
how can a priority queue protect critical work while avoiding indefinite starvation of other classes?
why can equal source and target row counts fail to prove migration completeness?
which queue disciplines and resource controls does the v12 checkout engine model?

during an orchestration control-plane outage, already-running containers keep answering requests, and the team concludes that the platform has high availability. why is that conclusion incomplete, and what must the availability claim and its failure test separate?
which scenario inputs must remain aligned to compare checkout candidates fairly?
what happens to the timeout when the v12 discrete-event model retries an attempt?
why can a metric label such as a tenant identifier multiply storage and query cost even when request volume is unchanged, and what should carry the per-tenant detail instead?

the v12 sensitivity screen reports arrival rate first-order 0.361 and total-order 0.464, and service mean 0.536 and 0.639. both total-minus-first gaps are 0.103, and the two first-order shares sum to 0.897. why is the repeated 0.103 not a coincidence, and what does it represent?
why does the atlas allow permissive mutual tls during a migration instead of requiring strict mutual tls from the start?
when a caller submits an unauthorized document id copied from a citation, why is omitting that document from ranked results insufficient, and what else must the service deny?

the v12 order-intake model fixes a 0.1-second integration step in its model contract instead of leaving it to the engine. why must the step be a declared model input, and how can a coarse step produce behavior that is only an artifact?
why can an index that helps a uniform workload make the same query slower after one tenant's rows become skewed?
how did linkedin’s kafka audit compare message counts along its multi-cluster path?
why does candidate c, with two attempts and linear backoff, show higher retry amplification and a higher timeout rate than candidate b?

a service reports 99.98% availability for the month with most of its error budget unspent, so the team treats a canary that occasionally double-books a seat as acceptable until the budget is exhausted. why is that reading wrong, and what must a budget-triggered release decision check before treating the canary as safe?

a 99.9% monthly target still has error budget left when a release starts timing out, and no single sustained-window alert has fired. why can the remaining budget and the quiet alert both fail to stop the release, and how should short and long burn windows be used instead?
what distinction separates verification of a simulation engine from validation for a decision?
what makes a scenario metric comparable between candidates with different server counts?
what transient read behavior can remain immediately after a cache invalidation on write?
when should a v12 decision remain unsupported even though a model run converges?
why can the v12 decision-validity gate not compensate for a failed statistical gate, and what outcome follows for a recommendation built on an unconverged run?

a catalogue serves each item from a local in-process cache in front of a shared cache, and the shared tier uses stale-while-revalidate with a 60-second stale window. a writer commits a new version and invalidates only the shared key, while a reader that began before the write repopulates that key from its older snapshot. why can a later reader still see a value older than either tier's declared freshness bound, and what must each tier and each fill record before the design may claim that bound?
what evidence makes an extracted dependency edge traceable to its source?

a client sends only the highest commit position it has observed to whichever replica answers. after a leader change, why can a replica whose applied position is numerically higher still return a state that violates read-your-writes, and what must the token and the routing decision carry instead?
why might promoting a streaming replica fail to recover an accidental deletion?
why can a query be badly costed when both correlated columns have current statistics, and what has to happen before new extended statistics change the plan?
in discord’s search-indexing case, why could a healthy search shard still miss messages after an outage?
how did discord’s data-service layer reduce redundant reads for a hot message channel?

a team proposes replacing a small self-managed deployment with a managed service because its monthly instance fee is lower. why can total lifecycle cost still rise, and what must be compared on the same horizon before treating the cheaper fee as evidence?
why does one general-purpose api become a poor fit for materially different clients, and what must a per-client backend avoid becoming?

a v12 decision record has status insufficient-evidence and recommendation none, and an analyst adds the least-bad recommendation so the record looks complete. why is that a contract failure rather than an improvement?
